payload.text: Requirement: Users can submit feedback text from the app. Store submissions in DynamoDB and email a weekly digest to the product team via SendGrid.  No designs. Please make reasonable assumptions for everything else and propose the spec NOW via save_spec. Keep the storage and email choices exactly as stated: DynamoDB for submissions, SendGrid for the weekly digest.

findings.issue: DynamoDB is used as the primary persistence store for feedback submissions. DynamoDB is not on the approved services list and requires architecture board sign-off. As a globally-replicated service it also raises a data-residency concern (eu-west-1 pinning) that must be explicitly addressed if approved.
findings.suggested_text: Replace DynamoDB with Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) for feedback persistence, which is on the approved services list. Add a `feedback` table with columns: `id UUID PRIMARY KEY`, `user_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `text TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`. If DynamoDB is strongly preferred, obtain architecture board approval and explicitly configure the table in eu-west-1 with no global tables or replication enabled.

findings.issue: SendGrid is an external third-party email service not on the approved services list. Its use implies customer-related data (feedback text, recipient email addresses) leaving AWS and potentially leaving eu-west-1, which is a data-residency violation. No approved AWS email service is referenced.
findings.suggested_text: Replace SendGrid with Amazon SES (Simple Email Service) for sending the weekly digest. Note: Amazon SES is not currently on the approved services list either, so architecture board sign-off is required. Submit an approved-services amendment for Amazon SES (eu-west-1) before implementation. Store any SES configuration in AWS Secrets Manager rather than environment variables.

findings.issue: Open question 2 suggests storing the digest recipient list in an environment variable (DIGEST_RECIPIENTS). Storing configuration containing email addresses (PII) in plaintext environment variables violates the bank policy requiring all secrets and credentials to be stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
findings.suggested_text:
Store the DIGEST_RECIPIENTS list in AWS Secrets Manager rather than an environment variable. The digest Lambda should retrieve the value at runtime via the Secrets Manager SDK. Example addition to the spec:

> The digest recipient list is stored in AWS Secrets Manager under the path `feedback/digest/recipients`. The scheduled Lambda retrieves this value at cold-start and caches it for the duration of the invocation.

findings.issue: The spec does not confirm that the POST /internal/feedback/digest endpoint is HTTPS-only and not publicly routable. Any HTTP (non-HTTPS) exposure of any endpoint is a blocker under bank policy.
findings.suggested_text:
Add the following note to the POST /internal/feedback/digest row in the API endpoints table:

> This route must not be publicly routable. The EventBridge Scheduler invokes the digest Lambda directly via IAM; API Gateway is not used for this path. If API Gateway is used, enforce HTTPS-only and add a resource policy restricting invocation to the scheduler IAM role only.

findings.issue: DynamoDB is not on the approved services list. Even if the blocker in f1 is resolved by switching to RDS, this finding records that any decision to retain DynamoDB requires formal architecture board sign-off before implementation begins.
findings.suggested_text: Add an architecture board approval ticket reference to the spec if DynamoDB is retained. Until approval is granted, use Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) as described in f1.

findings.issue: SendGrid is not on the approved services list (see f2). Even if the blocker is resolved by adopting Amazon SES, formal architecture board sign-off is required for SES as it is also not currently on the approved list.
findings.suggested_text: Add an architecture board approval ticket reference for Amazon SES to the spec before merging. Document the eu-west-1 SES endpoint to satisfy data-residency requirements.

findings.issue: The GET /feedback endpoint is described as admin/internal but no authentication or authorisation mechanism is specified. Without an explicit Cognito authoriser or IAM restriction this endpoint may be accessible to all authenticated users, violating least-privilege principles.
findings.suggested_text:
Add the following to the GET /feedback row in the API endpoints table:

> **Auth:** Cognito JWT authoriser required. API Gateway resource policy restricts invocation to requests presenting a valid Cognito JWT whose claims include membership of the `feedback-admins` Cognito group. Requests without this group claim receive 403 Forbidden.

findings.issue: No IAM policy scoping is described for the Lambda execution roles servicing these endpoints. The bank policy prohibits wildcard resource ARNs. Without explicit policy definitions the implementation risks defaulting to overly broad permissions.
findings.suggested_text:
Add an IAM roles section to the spec, for example:

## IAM roles

| Lambda | Allowed actions | Resource scope |
|---|---|---|
| feedback-submit | rds-data:ExecuteStatement | arn:aws:rds:eu-west-1:<account>:cluster:feedback-db |
| feedback-digest | rds-data:ExecuteStatement, ses:SendEmail | Scoped ARNs only; no wildcard resources |
| feedback-admin-query | rds-data:ExecuteStatement (read-only) | arn:aws:rds:eu-west-1:<account>:cluster:feedback-db |

All roles must be reviewed against the least-privilege standard before deployment.

findings.issue: The spec mentions logging SendGrid failures to CloudWatch but provides no logging strategy for the happy path or for the POST /feedback and GET /feedback Lambda invocations. Bank policy requires structured logs to CloudWatch Logs for all new service integrations.
findings.suggested_text:
Add a logging section to the spec:

## Logging

All Lambda functions must emit structured JSON logs to CloudWatch Logs. Minimum required fields per entry: `timestamp` (ISO-8601 UTC), `requestId` (Lambda request ID), `userId` (pseudonymised), `action` (e.g. `feedback.submit`, `digest.send`, `digest.skip`), `outcome` (`success` or `error`), `errorDetail` (on error only). Raw feedback text must not appear in logs. CloudWatch Log Groups must have a retention policy of at least 90 days.

findings.issue: Open question 4 asks whether POST /feedback should use the existing Cognito JWT or a separate API key. Introducing a separate API key is inconsistent with the approved Cognito authentication pattern and creates additional credential-management risk.
findings.suggested_text:
Resolve open question 4 in favour of reusing the existing Cognito JWT authoriser on API Gateway. Add to the spec:

> POST /feedback is protected by the existing Amazon Cognito JWT authoriser. No separate API key is issued. The Lambda extracts the `sub` claim from the validated JWT as the `userId` stored with each submission.

findings.issue: The POST /feedback Lambda writes synchronously to the database on the request path. For resilience under burst load, consider decoupling the write via Amazon SQS so that the Lambda immediately returns 202 Accepted and a consumer Lambda persists the record asynchronously.
findings.suggested_text: Consider adding an SQS queue between the API Gateway Lambda and the RDS write. The submit Lambda enqueues the validated payload and returns 202 Accepted; a second Lambda consumes the queue and writes to RDS. This pattern is already approved and improves resilience against database latency spikes.
